what: Human ratings of the image → Ether creature closure run (real-extract.json → <id>/source.png, author-8.png, judge-8.png, author-12.png, judge-12.png, ether-1…5.jpg, noreveal-complete.jpg). Rated by looking. image = the gpt-image-2 picture as a creative source; recognition = the completed eight-light Ether figure read WITHOUT the picture (judge-8.png / ether-2-complete.png); unfinished = the gap as a mystery (does the missing join read as something to do, and is the creature still recognisable without it); reveal = the accepted reveal suggestions at their default size against no reveal (A transformative · B meaningful · C weak · D unnecessary); alive = the completion → awakening → roaming loop in the real sky; overall A–D.
labels: Every row: REAL MODEL — the picture by gpt-image-2 (streamed), the extraction by gpt-4.1 with the actual picture attached; nothing constructed, nothing substituted. Everything RESEARCH ONLY; nothing reaches production.

results.reveal_note: one supported reveal landed at eight (STAR HAIR as a contour); it is faint against the tail, which the figure already carries

The picture is the best of the seven and the figure the second weakest.

against_v2: The V2 closure run (shots/closure/ratings.json) graded A0 B2 C4 D3 on nine creatures with the compiler; this run grades A0 B5 C2 D0 on seven with the picture read directly. No D anywhere, and the two C's are the two creatures whose species lives in an outline (a dragon's wing, a lion's mane) that eight lights cannot hold — the same ceiling the eight-point study found by hand.
verdict: GOOD ENOUGH TO MOVE FORWARD, with two things named. The simplest bridge works: gpt-image-2 draws a readable single creature every time (7/7 A), gpt-4.1 reads the actual picture into points that sit ON the creature (14/14 valid at eight and twelve; 12 of 14 on the first attempt, the other two on the second once the proxy's model_not_found is retried), and the existing Ether runtime completes, awakens and roams every one of the seven at eight lights with no production change. The figures are honest silhouettes rather than tangles — the extraction's lights are where the creature is, which is the thing no compiler managed. Named: (1) at eight lights a wing's outline and a mane cannot be held, so dragon and winged lion stay at C until the production budget question is decided; (2) the model lists missing connections SEPARATELY from connections (13 of 14 replies were repaired on the record — the model's gaps were added as connections and then left missing — and one of its gaps would have stranded a point and was kept as a connection instead; the falcon's two gaps at eight are the Lab's own), and the reveal defaults are sized in frame units and come out oversized — both are Lab-side, both are recorded, neither is a reason to keep the compiler.
